::: {#rem-sets-of-sets}
#### Sets can be elements of sets

The elements of a set can themselves be sets.
For example, $S = \set{\set{1, 2}, 3, \set{3}}$ has three elements:
the set $\set{1, 2}$, the number $3$, and the set $\set{3}$.
So $\set{1, 2} \in S$, but $1 \notin S$,
because $1$ is an element of an element of $S$, not an element of $S$.
And $3 \ne \set{3}$: one is a number, and the other is a set with one element.
So $\abs{S} = 3$ (@def-cardinality).

:::
